title: Sounding natural
goal: React like a local (really? no way! amazing!), use tag questions and the little words ہی, تو, نا, use echo words like چائے وائے, and keep a conversation going when you don't understand something.
intro:
You can have perfect grammar and still sound like a textbook. What makes Urdu sound *alive* is the small stuff: **سچی؟**, **ہو ہی نہیں سکتا!**, **تم بھی نا!**, **چائے وائے پیو گے؟** This unit is all small stuff.

You'll learn the **tag** نا 'right?', the **emphatic particles** ہی and تو that change the whole tone of a sentence, **echo words** (کام وام 'work and stuff'), and the survival phrases for when someone talks too fast or uses a word you don't know. You'll also see how people slip English into Urdu — because everyone does.

vocab.note: سچی؟ really? / seriously? Also سچ میں؟ More careful: واقعی؟
Friends only. Stronger: اللہ قسم / خدا قسم.
Praise or delight: واہ، کیا بات ہے! Said sarcastically too: واہ جی واہ!
Said on hearing good news or praising someone — and to ward off the evil eye.
lit. it is evident
Among friends affectionate: پاگل ہو کیا؟ are you mad? Not for elders.
چپ کرو shut up / be quiet (rude unless joking); چپ ہو جانا to fall silent
An echo pair from ٹھیک: کھانا ٹھیک ٹھاک تھا the food was OK. Also 'well and fine': سب ٹھیک ٹھاک ہے.
Comes right after the word it stresses. Fuses: یہ + ہی = یہی, وہ + ہی = وہی, اب + ہی = ابھی, تب + ہی = تبھی.
تبھی تو! no wonder! (lit. only then)
Same as اصل میں; good for softening a no: دراصل، آج میں مصروف ہوں.
Comes at the end of a list: کپڑے، جوتے وغیرہ.
The first is idhar 'here', the second udhar 'there' — same spelling.
An echo pair from سچ: کیا تم سچ مچ گئے؟ did you really go?
f/m · وہ اس ٹائپ کا بندہ نہیں he's not that type. More careful: قسم qism (f).
آہستہ آہستہ gradually, little by little
ذرا دہرا دیں؟ could you repeat that?
m · pl الفاظ (formal) — in speech also لفظ
From سمجھنا 'to understand' — lit. to make understand.
Short for بھائی, used to anyone, male or female, among friends and family: بھئی، بتاؤ تو!
Small mishaps and mild annoyance: اوہو، میں بھول گیا!
Pain, longing or affection: ہائے، کتنا پیارا! Common among women and in songs.
Shock or disapproval, often doubled: توبہ توبہ!

grammar.title: Tag questions: نا and ہے نا
grammar.body:
English has dozens of tags (isn't it? don't you? won't they?). Urdu mostly has one: **نا** nā at the end of the sentence, with a rising tone — 'right?':

تم کل آ رہے ہو **نا**؟ 'You're coming tomorrow, right?'
تم نے کھانا کھا لیا ہے **نا**؟ 'You've eaten, haven't you?'

**ہے نا؟** is added after a whole statement as a separate tag, and stays ہے even if the statement is in the past: کھانا اچھا تھا، **ہے نا**؟ 'The food was good, wasn't it?'

**نہیں؟** 'no?' also works as a tag, especially when you're less sure: وہ تمہاری کزن ہے، **نہیں**؟

**نا with commands** isn't a question at all — it softens and coaxes: بتاؤ **نا**! 'come on, tell me!', آ جاؤ **نا** 'do come'. With آپ: آپ بھی چلیں **نا**. And **تم بھی نا!** 'oh, you!' is pure fond exasperation.

**Spelling trap:** **نا** (nā, long) is the tag; **نہ** (na, short) means 'not' (in subjunctives, conditionals and 'neither… nor'). Many people mix up the spellings in texts, but the sounds differ.

examples.native: تم کل آ رہے ہو نا؟
examples.roman: tum kal ā rahe ho nā?

examples.en: Come on, tell me — what happened?

grammar.title: Emphasis: ہی, تو and بھی
grammar.body:
Three little particles change the tone of a whole sentence. Each comes **right after** the word it affects.

**ہی** hī — 'only, just, the very':
آج **ہی** 'today itself / only today', میں **ہی** 'me and nobody else', پہلے **ہی** 'already'. In negatives it means 'just not / not at all': ہو **ہی** نہیں سکتا 'it simply can't be', کبھی بتایا **ہی** نہیں 'never even said'. It fuses with some words: **یہی** (this very), **وہی** (that very, the same), **ابھی** (right now), **تبھی** (no wonder), **یہیں / وہیں** (right here / there).

**تو** to (short o — not تو tū 'you') — 'as for, well, really':
- contrast: میں **تو** نہیں جا رہا 'well, *I'm* not going' (whatever others do)
- emphasis: یہی **تو** مسئلہ ہے 'that's exactly the problem'; یہ **تو** کمال ہے 'now *that's* amazing'
- urging: دیکھو **تو**! 'just look!'

**بھی** bhī — 'also', and 'even / at all' after question words: **کچھ بھی** 'anything (at all)', **کوئی بھی** 'anyone', **کبھی بھی** 'ever, any time', **پھر بھی** 'even so'.

**Trap:** don't scatter them. One ہی or تو per sentence, on the word that matters, is what natives do.

examples.native: میں نے تو پہلے ہی کہا تھا!
examples.roman: maiṃ ne to pahle hī kahā thā!

examples.native: وہ آج ہی واپس آیا ہے۔

examples.native: کچھ بھی کھا لو، سب مزیدار ہے۔
examples.roman: kuchh bhī khā lo, sab mazedār hai.

examples.native: دیکھو تو، کتنا پیارا بچہ ہے!
examples.roman: dekho to, kitnā pyārā bachcha hai!
examples.en: Just look, what a sweet baby!

grammar.title: Echo words and doubled words
grammar.body:
**Echo words:** repeat a word with its first sound replaced by **و** v, and it means 'X and stuff like that / X or anything':

**چائے وائے** 'tea or something', **کام وام** 'work and all that', **پیسے ویسے** 'money and that', **کھانا وانا** 'food and so on'. A word that starts with a vowel just gets **و** in front: **انڈے ونڈے** 'eggs and things'.

The tone is casual and often a bit dismissive: **شادی وادی** کا کوئی ارادہ نہیں 'no plans for marriage or any of that'. Only the first word inflects normally; the echo copies it.

**Doubled words:** repeating a word intensifies or spreads it: **جلدی جلدی** 'quick, quick', **آہستہ آہستہ** 'little by little', **گرم گرم** 'piping hot', **کبھی کبھی** 'sometimes', **کیا کیا** 'what all (things)'.

**Fixed pairs:** **ٹھیک ٹھاک** 'all right', **ادھر ادھر** 'here and there', **آس پاس** 'around', **گپ شپ** 'chit-chat'. And to end a list: **وغیرہ** 'etc.'.

examples.native: آج کام وام چھوڑو، باہر چلتے ہیں۔
examples.roman: āj kām vām chhoṛo, bāhar chalte haiṃ.
examples.en: Forget work and all that today — let's go out.

examples.native: مجھے شادی وادی میں کوئی دلچسپی نہیں۔
examples.roman: mujhe shādī vādī meṃ koī dilchaspī nahīṃ.
examples.en: I'm not interested in marriage and all that.

examples.roman: āhista āhista sab samajh ā jā’e gā.
examples.en: Little by little you'll understand it all.

dialogue.title: Doodh patti in Karachi
dialogue.setting: Sara, who grew up in Manchester, is visiting her cousin Faraz in Karachi. They've stopped at a roadside tea stall.

lines.speaker: Faraz
lines.native: تو، کراچی کیسا لگا؟ سچ بتانا۔
lines.roman: to, Karāchī kaisā lagā? sach batānā.
lines.en: So, how are you finding Karachi? Be honest.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: Amazing! Just the heat… good grief!

lines.speaker: Faraz
lines.native: ہاہا، ابھی تو اکتوبر ہے! جون میں آتیں تو پتا چلتا۔

lines.en: Ha, it's only October! If you'd come in June, then you'd know.

lines.roman: sachchī? is se bhī zyāda? ho hī nahīṃ saktā!
lines.en: Seriously? Even hotter than this? No way!

lines.speaker: Faraz

lines.roman: qasam se. achchhā, chā’e vā’e piyo gī? yahāṃ kī dūdh pattī kamāl hai.
lines.en: I swear. Anyway — want some tea or something? The doodh patti here is amazing.

lines.speaker: Sara

lines.roman: dūdh pattī? ek minaṭ… is kā matlab kyā hai?
lines.en: Doodh patti? Hang on… what does that mean?

lines.speaker: Faraz
lines.native: یعنی وہ چائے جو صرف دودھ میں بنتی ہے، پانی کے بغیر۔

lines.en: I mean tea that's made just in milk, no water.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.native: اچھا، تبھی تو اتنی گاڑھی اور میٹھی ہے!
lines.roman: achchhā, tabhī to itnī gāṛhī aur mīṭhī hai!
lines.en: Oh, no wonder it's so thick and sweet!

lines.speaker: Faraz
lines.native: ویسے تمہاری اردو کافی بہتر ہو گئی ہے۔ کس سے سیکھی؟
lines.roman: vaise tumhārī urdū kāfī behtar ho ga’ī hai. kis se sīkhī?
lines.en: By the way, your Urdu's got much better. Who taught you?

lines.speaker: Sara

lines.roman: nānī se… aur ḍrāmoṃ se! lekin tum log bahut tez bolte ho.
lines.en: Nani… and dramas! But you lot talk so fast.

lines.speaker: Faraz
lines.native: ارے، تم نے کبھی بتایا ہی نہیں! میں آہستہ بول دیتا۔
lines.roman: are, tum ne kabhī batāyā hī nahīṃ! maiṃ āhista bol detā.
lines.en: Hey, you never even said! I'd have spoken slowly.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.native: رہنے دو، تم آہستہ بولو گے تو میں بور ہو جاؤں گی!
lines.roman: rahne do, tum āhista bolo ge to maiṃ bor ho jā’ūṃ gī!
lines.en: Don't bother — if you talk slowly I'll get bored!

lines.speaker: Faraz
lines.native: تم بھی نا! چلو بھائی، دو دودھ پتی، اور ساتھ میں گرم گرم سموسے۔

culture:
**Mixing English** into Urdu is completely normal in cities and among young people: *actually*, *basically*, *I mean*, *so*, *seriously* slide into Urdu sentences, and most technical, office and pop-culture words are English with Urdu verbs (*plan* کرنا, *cancel* ہو گیا). You won't sound less fluent by doing it — you'll sound local. Older people and formal settings lean more towards pure Urdu.

**Reactions** carry a lot of weight. Listeners keep the speaker going with **جی جی**, **ہاں جی**, **اچھا؟**, **پھر؟**. Good news gets **واہ!** or **ماشاءاللہ**; small mishaps **اوہو**; shock **توبہ** (said seriously by older people, jokingly by the young); affection **ہائے**. Words like **پاگل**, **بکواس**, **چپ کرو** and **قسم سے** are for friends — never for elders or strangers.

**Regional colour:** in Lahore you'll hear Punjabi mixed in (کی حال اے؟ 'how's it going?'); Karachi has its own slang (**ابے یار**, between close friends only). Asking **اس کو اردو میں کیا کہتے ہیں؟** delights people — expect a long, happy explanation.

tip.title: Reacting
tip.body:
- Surprise: **سچی؟** really? · **مذاق کر رہے ہو؟** kidding? · **ہو ہی نہیں سکتا!** no way!
- Good news: **واہ!** · **کیا بات ہے!** · **کمال ہے!** · **زبردست!**
- Swearing it's true: **قسم سے** — with friends only.

tip.title: Right? = نا
tip.body:
- Add **نا** at the end for 'right? / isn't it?': تم آ رہی ہو **نا**؟
- After a whole statement: **ہے نا؟** — always ہے, even after a past: اچھا تھا، **ہے نا**؟
- With a command, نا coaxes: بولو **نا**! 'come on, say it!'
- Don't confuse **نا** (tag) with **نہ** (not).

tip.title: ہی, تو, بھی
tip.body:
- **ہی** 'only / the very': کل **ہی** 'only yesterday'; fused: **یہی**, **وہی**, **تبھی**.
- **تو** (to) 'as for / really': میں **تو** نہیں جا رہا 'well, *I'm* not going'; دیکھو **تو**! 'just look!'
- **بھی** after question words = 'at all': **کچھ بھی**, **کبھی بھی**.
- Put it right after the word you stress.

sentences.native: ہم تو کل ہی آئے ہیں۔

sentences.en: We only got here yesterday.

sentences.en: Just look who's here!

sentences.en: Well, I'm not going — you go.

sentences.en: He's never, ever on time.

sentences.roman: darasl, mujhe āj kuchh kām hai.
sentences.en: Actually, I've got something on today.

tip.title: Echo words: چائے وائے
tip.body:
- Repeat a word with **و** at the start = 'and stuff': **چائے وائے** tea or something, **پیسے ویسے** money and all that.
- Doubling intensifies: **جلدی جلدی** quick quick, **گرم گرم** piping hot.
- Fixed pairs: **ادھر ادھر**, **ٹھیک ٹھاک**. End a list with **وغیرہ**.

lessons.title: Sorry, say that again?

tip.title: When you don't follow
tip.body:
- **جی؟** or **ایک بار پھر کہیے؟** = pardon? / say that again?
- **ذرا آہستہ بولیں** = slower, please; **ذرا دہرا دیں** = could you repeat it?
- Lost a word? Say **وہ کیا کہتے ہیں…** and describe it: **جہاں / جو / جس سے…**
- Ask: **اس کا مطلب کیا ہے؟** / **سمجھا دیں؟**

tip.title: Little noises that say a lot
tip.body:
- **ارے** hey! / oh! · **اوہو** oh no, oops · **ہائے** aww / ouch · **توبہ توبہ** good grief!
- **عجیب بات ہے** that's strange · **حد ہو گئی!** this is ridiculous!
- **اچھا خاصا** 'quite' agrees: **اچھی خاصی** انگریزی.
- English fillers (*basically*, *actually*) are fine — everyone uses them.
